answer: It writes no agent program of its own and bundles none. It runs the vendors' programs, unmodified. It never chooses or switches a model. It does no orchestration. A file crosses between two computers only by a rule you set; Silo carries nothing else between agents. It builds no window for talking to an agent: an answer to an ask or to an agent's question, and a comment on what a turn changed, are all you send it from Silo. It does not hide or wrap the agent program's own interface. It builds no board for tracking work. It is not a memory system for agents. An agent's memory is the files of its computer.
